name: Recursion
definition: A programming technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of the same problem until reaching a terminating base condition.
common_confusion: Confusing the base case with loop termination or forgetting that each call maintains its own distinct execution stack frame.
simpler_explanation: Think of recursion like Russian nesting dolls (Matryoshka). You open each doll to find a smaller one until you reach the solid tiny doll inside (the base case). Then you close them back up.
visual_example: factorial(3) pushes factorial(2), which pushes factorial(1)=1, then returns unwind back up: 1 -> 2 -> 6.

name: Base Case
definition: The guard clause or stopping condition in a recursive function that directly returns a value without making any further recursive calls.
common_confusion: Placing the base case after the recursive invocation or using a condition that incoming arguments can never satisfy.
simpler_explanation: The base case is the emergency brake of your recursive function. It stops the chain reaction and hands back a real answer.

name: Call Stack
definition: A Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) runtime data structure that tracks active function calls, executing the topmost frame before returning to the caller.
common_confusion: Assuming functions execute in parallel rather than synchronously pausing until deeper frames return.
simpler_explanation: A stack of cafeteria trays. You put a new tray on top when a function is called, and you can only remove the top tray when that function finishes.

name: Stack Frame
definition: A dedicated memory block allocated on the call stack for an active function call, storing arguments, local variables, and the caller return address.
common_confusion: Believing variables with identical names across recursive invocations overwrite each other.
simpler_explanation: A personal notebook page created fresh for each function invocation holding its own private notes and variables.
visual_example: Frame 3: n=3, waiting on fact(2) | Frame 2: n=2, waiting on fact(1) | Frame 1: n=1, returns 1

name: Stack Overflow
definition: A runtime error that occurs when recursive calls exceed the maximum call stack memory boundary, usually caused by a missing base case.
common_confusion: Thinking the computer has exhausted total system RAM rather than exceeding the designated call stack depth.
simpler_explanation: Your tray stack grows so tall it hits the ceiling and crashes because the emergency brake never fired.
visual_example: 10,000 recursive frames stacked -> RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.

name: Functions
definition: A self-contained block of reusable code that accepts parameter inputs, performs defined logic, and returns an output value.
common_confusion: Confusing parameters (the declared variables in function definition) with arguments (actual values passed at runtime).
simpler_explanation: A kitchen blender recipe: you drop ingredients into the top, press run, and get a smoothie out of the spout.
visual_example: function multiply(a, b) { return a * b; }

name: Photosynthesis
definition: The biological process by which green plants and autotrophs convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into oxygen and glucose.
common_confusion: Assuming plants only release oxygen and do not perform cellular respiration with oxygen themselves.
simpler_explanation: Solar-powered cooking: sunlight + water + carbon dioxide = sugar + oxygen.

name: Calvin Cycle
definition: The light-independent set of chemical reactions occurring in the chloroplast stroma that fixes carbon dioxide into glucose using ATP and NADPH.
common_confusion: Assuming the cycle only occurs at night because it is named 'light-independent'.
simpler_explanation: The sugar assembly line in the chloroplast stroma running on batteries charged by sunlight.
